question.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-{x}^{2}{y}^{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-{x}^{2}{y}^{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y-2x{y}^{3} & x-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2x{y}^{3})=-2{y}^{3}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=1-6x{y}^{2} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2x{y}^{3})=1-6x{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=-6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2{y}^{3} & 1-6x{y}^{2} \\ 1-6x{y}^{2} & -6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,0).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
